target_audience: Computer Science, Computer Engineering and IT college students

concepts.name: Programming Fundamentals
concepts.description: Variables, types, control flow and functions.
concepts.lesson: Variables store values; data types define representations; conditions select branches; loops repeat operations; functions organize reusable logic.
concepts.worked_example: If x = 4 and x = x + 3, the new value of x is 7.
concepts.practice_hint: Trace each variable after every statement.

concepts.name: Data Structures
concepts.description: Arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists and trees.
concepts.lesson: Arrays support indexed access; stacks use LIFO; queues use FIFO; trees represent hierarchical data.
concepts.worked_example: Push 2 and then 5 onto a stack. The first value popped is 5.
concepts.practice_hint: Choose a structure based on the operations you need.

concepts.name: Algorithms and Complexity
concepts.lesson: Big-O describes how resource use grows with input size. Binary search requires sorted data and halves the search interval.
concepts.worked_example: Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search range.
concepts.practice_hint: Count how operations grow when the input size doubles.

concepts.name: Database Management Systems
concepts.lesson: Primary keys identify rows; foreign keys link tables; normalization reduces redundancy; transactions group operations reliably.
concepts.worked_example: An Enrollments table can reference Students using student_id.
concepts.practice_hint: Identify keys and repeated data before designing a schema.

concepts.name: Discrete Mathematics
concepts.description: Logic, sets, relations, counting and graphs.
concepts.lesson: Logic studies truth-valued statements; sets group distinct elements; graph theory models vertices and edges.
concepts.worked_example: If P is true and Q is false, P AND Q is false.
concepts.practice_hint: Use a truth table instead of guessing.

concepts.name: Operating Systems
concepts.description: Processes, threads, scheduling, memory and deadlocks.
concepts.lesson: Operating systems manage hardware and processes. Threads share process resources, and scheduling allocates CPU time.
concepts.worked_example: Round-robin scheduling gives each ready process a time quantum.
concepts.practice_hint: Trace process states and resource ownership.

questions.question: Which Python type represents True or False?
questions.explanation: The bool type represents Boolean truth values.

questions.question: What does a for loop commonly do?
questions.explanation: A for loop iterates over items.

questions.question: What is x after x = 4; x = x + 3?
questions.explanation: The new value is 4 plus 3.

questions.question: What is a main benefit of functions?
questions.explanation: Functions improve modularity and reuse.

questions.question: Which structure follows LIFO?
questions.explanation: A stack removes the newest item first.

questions.question: Which structure commonly follows FIFO?
questions.explanation: A queue removes items in insertion order.

questions.question: Which structure normally provides O(1) indexed access?
questions.explanation: Array indexing is constant time under the usual RAM model.

questions.question: Which BST traversal visits keys in sorted order?
questions.explanation: Inorder visits left subtree, node, then right subtree.

questions.question: What is the complexity of one pass through n items?
questions.explanation: The work grows linearly with input size.

questions.question: Binary search requires which condition?

options.C: Data is a linked list only

questions.explanation: Binary search uses sorted order to discard half the range.

questions.question: Checking every pair among n items is typically what complexity?
questions.explanation: The number of pairs grows quadratically.

questions.question: What is merge sort's usual time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge sort processes n items at each of log n levels.

questions.question: What does a primary key do?
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies a row.

questions.question: Which SQL command retrieves data?
questions.explanation: SELECT queries rows and columns.

questions.question: A foreign key primarily enforces what?
questions.explanation: Foreign keys link records and enforce referential integrity.

questions.question: Which ACID property means committed changes survive a crash?
questions.explanation: Durability preserves committed transactions.

questions.question: If P is true and Q false, what is P AND Q?
questions.explanation: AND is true only when both operands are true.

questions.question: A set is best described as what?
questions.explanation: A set contains distinct elements.

questions.question: An undirected graph edge connects what?
questions.explanation: An undirected edge represents a connection without direction.

questions.question: What is the contrapositive of If P then Q?

options.B: If not P then not Q
options.D: If not Q then not P

questions.explanation: The contrapositive is logically equivalent to the original implication.

questions.question: What is a process?

options.A: A running instance of a program

questions.explanation: A process is an executing program with its state and resources.

questions.question: Threads in the same process generally share what?
questions.explanation: Threads share the process address space and many resources.

questions.question: Round-robin scheduling gives each ready process what?
questions.explanation: Each ready process receives a bounded CPU time slice.

questions.question: Deadlock can occur when processes do what?

options.D: Wait indefinitely for resources held by one another

questions.explanation: Deadlock can occur when processes wait cyclically for resources.
